scope: Isolated S1 crash recovery of a document that a javascript: URL created. The experimental patch drops the javascript: URL result and its Content-Type header from every crash load, so a top-level crash load fetches Servo's error page and reload from that page fetches the document's URL. The javascript-url-crash-recovery case now asserts this behavior in both modes. The case count does not change. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: Crash recovery must not render a javascript: URL document's result again. The experimental engine patch must drop that result from the crash load. The crash document is then an error page, not page content, and reload must not render the result again (2026-11-26).
A failed view at about:blank relies on the product's native error state. The engine does not need to fetch Servo's error page for it (2026-11-26).

baseline.head: 38f2247
baseline.note: The frame containment evidence records three passing runs in each mode at 38f2247. origin/main was at 38f2247 when this work started.

configuration.crash_page_check: Each fetched crash document must contain the engine's failure reason. Servo's crash.html embeds that reason. The check only orders the fixture and grants no host authority.
configuration.containment_check: Each converted case holds the healthy parent's script thread at a barrier and queues eight mixed scoped and unscoped callbacks there. Inside the barrier, the host waits until the frame state probe shows that the failed pipeline is gone, and for a pending navigation that the old child pipeline is still current and live with no pending pipeline. It also waits for revocation of each other view in the failed event loop and then for 200 milliseconds. A revocation or crash notification of the parent also ends the wait, so the next check reports it. The parent must then have no terminal callback, no revocation, and no crash notification. After release, all eight callbacks must succeed in the parent's document. The frame state probe must then report a new, live frame pipeline whose crash details begin with the exact reason and no pending pipeline.
configuration.frame_state_probe: frame_state_for_document_scope_probe reads the constellation's record of the active top-level document's newest child frame: its current pipeline, whether that pipeline is live, its load data's crash details, and whether the frame has a pending pipeline. Page JavaScript cannot supply these values.
configuration.javascript_url_check: The fixture records, for each intercepted request of the javascript: URL source page, whether it carried a Content-Type request header. After the failure, the crash document must contain the exact reason, have the source page's URL and the origin null, have no fixture marker and no result text, and not run an inserted script. Only the initial source request may exist before reload. After reload, the fixture waits for either the source page's marker or the result's marker. The reloaded document must be the source page with the real origin, its own marker, no result text, no failure reason, and a running inserted script. Exactly two source requests must exist, and neither may carry a Content-Type header. The markers and request record only order and observe the fixture; they grant no host authority.

engine_patch.change: A new associated function, without_javascript_result, takes a crash load's base load data. If js_eval_result is set, it clears the result and removes the content-type header that evaluate_a_javascript_url added for the result's response. handle_panic_in_webview and contained_failed_frames build their crash loads from that base. A top-level crash load of a javascript: URL document therefore leaves the synchronous path in pre_page_load and fetches Servo's error page for the document's URL, which evaluate_a_javascript_url set to the source document's URL. The crash page's load data is the reload record, so the existing crash reload replacement in handle_reload_msg now loads the document's URL with the original sandboxing flags and no result. This matches Location::reload_without_origin_check, which reloads a live javascript: URL document by navigating to the window's URL with new load data and no result.
engine_patch.frame_path: A child frame's crash load already used the fetch path, so it never rendered a result. Its crash load data still kept the result, but no path removed the crash details from a frame's load: handle_reload_msg reads only the top-level pipeline, and history keeps the crash details when it rebuilds a page. The patch now drops the result from a frame's crash load as well. No fixture covers a javascript: URL document in a frame.

changes.name: Crash recovery rendered a javascript: URL result again
changes.observed: The crash load copied the failed pipeline's load data, including js_eval_result. pre_page_load loads any load data with a result synchronously and ignores the crash details, so the crash document rendered the result with the page's real origin and running scripts. The synchronous construction evidence characterized this behavior.
changes.fix: Every crash load drops the result. The crash document is now Servo's error page with the failure reason, the origin null, and no running scripts. The first negative control, the previous patch, fails at the converted case.

changes.name: Reload from the crash page rendered the result again
changes.observed: The crash reload replacement removes only the crash details from the crash page's load data, so the reload took the synchronous path with the result.
changes.fix: The crash page's load data no longer holds the result, so reload fetches the document's URL. The second negative control keeps the result in the load data and ignores it only for crash loads in the script thread. Its reload renders the result again.

changes.name: The reload request carried the result's Content-Type header
changes.observed: evaluate_a_javascript_url stores a Content-Type header for the result's response in the load's headers, which a fetch sends as request headers.
changes.fix: The crash load drops that header with the result. The third negative control keeps the header, and the reload request carries it.

findings: The crash document of a javascript: URL document is Servo's error page with the exact reason. Its URL is the source page's URL, its origin is null, it has no fixture marker and no result text, and an inserted script does not run.
The crash fetch skips embedder interception, so the host sees only the initial source request before reload.

Reload gives a new identity and rejects the crash document's scope. The reloaded document is the source page with the real origin and running scripts. It contains no result text and no failure reason.
The reload is a second request for the source page. Neither request carries a Content-Type header.
Revocation before eight terminal callbacks, released captures, rejection of the retained reply, recovery through a new URL, and an independent view's scope pass as before.
The behavior is the same in both modes.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
No fixture covers a javascript: URL document in a child frame, or one whose source document was at about:blank. The latter's crash load now takes the synchronous about:blank path.

The reload keeps the rest of the failed load's data, including the source document's policy container as the request client's container. An ordinary script-thread reload uses new load data without it. No fixture checks a policy effect on the reload request.

Recovery marks inactive history entries for reload with their own load data. The source shows that an inactive javascript: URL entry keeps its result, so back would render that result again, as a history rebuild after eviction would. No fixture checks this path.
